fix_commit.message: Prevent embedded 0x00 characters in the output strings from confusing the completion extension and causing it to read past the end of an array. [forum:/forumpost/88a08b3201|Forum post 88a08b3201].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Out-of-bounds read via mismatched nPrefix/nLine byte counts with embedded NUL characters in completion extension
findings.message: In `completionFilter()`, `pCur->nPrefix` and `pCur->nLine` are initialized via `sqlite3_value_bytes()`, which returns the full byte length of the SQLite value including any embedded 0x00 (NUL) bytes. However, the corresponding strings are then copied with `sqlite3_mprintf("%s", sqlite3_value_text(...))`, which stops copying at the first NUL character, producing a shorter string. This creates a mismatch: `nPrefix` (or `nLine`) may be larger than `strlen(zPrefix)` (or `strlen(zLine)`). Downstream code in `completionNext()` then uses these oversized length fields — in `sqlite3_strnicmp(pCur->zPrefix, ..., pCur->nPrefix)` — reading past the end of the actual NUL-terminated string. Additionally, the backward scan `while( i>0 && ... pCur->zLine[i-1]=='_' )` starting from `i = pCur->nLine` will access `zLine` beyond its actual length when `nLine > strlen(zLine)`, also causing an out-of-bounds read.
findings.suggestion: After copying via sqlite3_mprintf("%s", ...), recalculate nPrefix and nLine using strlen() on the copied string to account for any embedded NUL characters truncating the copy. Apply the same correction wherever nPrefix is derived from nLine arithmetic.

ground_truth.root_cause: The code uses `sqlite3_value_bytes()` to obtain byte counts (inclusive of embedded NULs) but copies the string text with a `%s` format specifier that stops at the first NUL character. There is no subsequent correction of the stored length field to match the actual copied string length, creating a length/content mismatch exploitable for out-of-bounds reads.
